# Quotation with attribution

Model: `quotation`. Each call creates a complete slide. Inter and text sizes stay fixed; quotation panel height follows measured text.

[Model index](../../../templates/MODELS.md) · [Palette and content guide](../../STUDIO-MODELS.md)

```latex
\studiosetup{palette=light}
\studiotemplate[variant=layered]{quotation}
```

Palette switches are available only where the original composition exists in both colours.
Unsupported explicit choices fail. A global palette leaves special compositions in their native treatment.

## Variants and named fields

Write bare text in `quote` and `attribution`. Double quotation marks and the em dash before the source are inserted automatically and included in panel measurement. Empty fields produce no stray punctuation.

### layered

Original palettes: blue.

[Current source](../../../templates/studio/chat-dialogue.tex) · [Full slot guide](../guides/chat-dialogue.md)

| Field | Default | Available space |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `quote` | <code>A clear quotation can highlight one idea while keeping its source in a separate field.</code> | Text width is panel width minus 178 units; measured text height. Centered layered panel, fixed padding, maximum height 1300. |
| `attribution` | <code>Source or reference</code> | Text width is panel width minus 178 units; measured text height. Centered layered panel, fixed padding, maximum height 1300. |

Layout options: `width=standard` (choice). See the full slot guide for supported values.

Choose width=compact, medium, standard or wide. Empty quotation fields use no measured text height; the panel adapts to the remaining content. See [quotation usage](../../STUDIO-DIALOGUES.md) for capacity and examples.

## Complete one-slide example

```latex
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{beamer}
\usetheme{bitpolito-studio}
\usepackage{bitpolitostudiotemplates}
\usepackage[backend=biber]{biblatex}
\addbibresource{bibliography.bib}
\begin{document}
\studiotemplate[
  variant={layered},
  palette={blue},
  quote={A clear quotation can highlight one idea while keeping its source in a separate field.},
  attribution={Source or reference}
]{quotation}
\end{document}
```
